hook: Hand-me-down dresser? Fixed bins won't fit it

scenes.visual_prompt: Odd-width secondhand dresser drawer with visible gaps where standard bins don't reach the edges
scenes.voiceover: If your dresser's a hand-me-down or an odd width, fixed bins are a gamble.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands folding and unfolding plastic-coated fabric divider panels, showing flexibility
scenes.voiceover: Delamu's dividers are eight foldable panels that expand to match your exact drawer width.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split screen: same drawer arranged with more small compartments, then rearranged with fewer larger ones
scenes.voiceover: Rearrange them as your baby grows, more small sections for socks now, fewer big ones for pants later.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand pressing down on folded jeans stacked in a compartment, panel not bowing under weight
scenes.voiceover: The semi-rigid material holds folded jeans and rompers without caving in.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a small dent in a foam-core divider wall after repeated overstuffing
scenes.voiceover: One thing to watch, the foam-core walls can dent if you stuff rolled clothes in too tight. Fold, don't roll.

caption: If your baby's dresser is a hand-me-down or just an odd size, the Delamu Foldable Drawer Dividers ($19.99) are the pick — 8 panels that expand into 8 to 15 compartments to match your drawer exactly. They resize as your baby grows out of the newborn stage. Full 5-way comparison linked in bio.
